indications.reason: One flu vaccine every year is recommended for all adults.

contraindications.text: A severe allergic reaction (such as anaphylaxis) after a previous dose of any flu vaccine.

precautions.text: Guillain-Barré syndrome within 6 weeks after a previous dose of any flu vaccine.
A moderate or severe illness right now, with or without fever.

content.disease: Flu can cause fever and chills, sore throat, muscle aches, tiredness, cough, headache, and a runny or stuffy nose.
content.why: Flu viruses change, and protection fades, so a new dose is recommended every season.
content.who: All adults aged 19 and older. For adults 65 and older, CDC lists high-dose, recombinant or adjuvanted flu vaccines as preferred.
content.catch_up: If you missed a dose this season, it can still be given while flu is circulating. Ask a pharmacist or clinic.
common_reactions: Soreness, redness or swelling where the shot was given
serious_reactions: There may be a very small increased risk of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) after inactivated flu vaccine.
A severe allergic reaction is very rare.
